question: On 19 September 2023, Azerbaijan launched an offensive that led to the capture of the Armenian enclave, the forced evacuation of the Armenian population and the destruction of churches and other buildings reminiscent of Armenian culture. In the same month, the Union donated EUR 5 million to the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) in response to the crisis in Nagorno-Karabakh.

The EU has maintained a partnership agreement with Azerbaijan since 1999. In October, the EU deployed monitoring experts at the Armenia-Azerbaijan border, the aim being to restore peace in the area, establish trust and demarcate the international border.
Azerbaijan has turned out to be an extremely unreliable partner which, by means of a war of aggression, has captured and ethnically cleansed a population’s historical homeland. 1.
Has the Commission received the ICRC’s report on how the humanitarian aid donation was spent?
What steps has the Commission taken to review relations with Azerbaijan and suspend the partnership agreement?
What further support does the Commission anticipate for the displaced population of NagornoKarabakh, such as redirecting development funds?
answer: 1. The Commission swiftly mobilised more than EUR 12 million in September 2023 in humanitarian aid to address the most urgent humanitarian needs in Armenia and inside Nagorno-Karabakh, out of which EUR 2.65 million to the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC). The support consists of cash assistance, shelter, food and non-food items, psychological support and protection.

As such, the ICRC reports on the use of funds to the Commission according to its contractual obligations. 2. The EU’s objectives are to promote security, stability and peace in the South Caucasus and to continue cooperation with the respective countries in the region on a bilateral and regional basis.
The EU attaches importance to continuing relations with Azerbaijan in various formats to reach these objectives, including through active engagement in the normalisation process.

At the same time, the High Representative/Vice-President condemned the military escalation and deplored loss of lives, calling for the immediate cessation of hostilities and on Azerbaijan to stop military activities in his X post of 19 September (1) and statement of 21 September 2023 (2). 3. On 13 February 2024, the Commission announced additional EUR 5.
5 million of humanitarian assistance to support the Armenians displaced from Nagorno-Karabakh.
